forecasts.question: Will at least 50 commercial vessels per day transit the Strait of Hormuz (50%+ of pre-war ~120/day baseline) during any consecutive 7-day window before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.38 → 0.14. PortWatch registered only 4 commercial transits on 2026-05-24 against a pre-crisis baseline of 95–130/day — under 5% of normal volume. Maersk, MSC, CMA CGM, and Hapag-Lloyd remain suspended. P&I war-risk insurance cancelled since March 5. 1,550+ vessels stranded. On May 27 the White House called an Iranian MOU leak ‘a complete fabrication’; Trump told cabinet he is ‘not satisfied with it yet’ and ‘won’t be rushed.’ Even a deal signed today cannot produce a 7-day sustained transit window of 50+/day within 13 remaining days given the insurance → carrier → repositioning mechanics required.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Hormuz Strait Monitor (or UNCTAD, or Lloyd’s List) reports ≥50 daily transits averaged over 7 consecutive days within the horizon window. NO if average stays below 50/day for the full horizon window.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Hormuz Strait Monitor (primary), Lloyd’s List Intelligence (secondary), UNCTAD Maritime Trade quarterly report (lagging confirmation).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If only Iranian-flagged or sanctions-evading dark-fleet vessels make up the count, but Western insurers still refuse: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. PGSA self-reported numbers are excluded from resolution sourcing. Third-country vessels count ONLY IF ≥2 of Hormuz Strait Monitor/Lloyd’s List/UNCTAD/Windward confirm them as independent commercial entities not under IRGC-linked tolls.

forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel confirmation. Polling alone does not resolve.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and the US confirm a signed written framework agreement (any named successor to the 14-point MOU) before EOD 2026-06-05?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.25 → 0.20. Trump stated May 23 the deal is ‘largely negotiated’; Pezeshkian said May 24 Iran is ‘ready to assure the world’ on nuclear intentions. However, on May 27 the White House called an Iranian state TV leak of MOU text ‘a complete fabrication’ and Trump told cabinet ‘not satisfied with it yet’ and ‘won’t be rushed.’ Key unresolved gaps: Hormuz sovereignty (Iran holds it retains management; US frames reopening as US-administered), nuclear sequencing, sanctions relief (‘no dust, no dollars’). The May 27 fabrication dispute is more recent and more dispositive than the May 23–24 optimism. Horizon EOD June 5 is 8 days away.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a named US administration official AND a named Iranian official publicly confirm a signed written framework (by any name); OR if the document text is published by Axios/Reuters/State Dept or Iran MFA with both parties acknowledging authenticity. Verbal ‘agreement in principle’ does not count.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: At minimum, Reuters AND one of Axios/AP/AFP quoting named US AND Iranian principals (not envoys alone). Official Iranian Foreign Ministry statement or State Dept press release also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Agreement by envoys only, without principal confirmation (Trump/Pezeshkian) within 72h of announcement = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If Iran signs but Khamenei’s office disavows within 72h = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. If Iran’s Supreme National Security Council formally blocks or delays implementation within 72h of signing = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will the Lebanon 45-day ceasefire extension (announced May 15) formally collapse — defined as US withdrawal of sponsorship OR Lebanese government publicly declaring the truce void — before EOD 2026-05-22?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED-NO. The 45-day ceasefire extension, confirmed by the US State Department on May 15, remained formally in place through EOD May 22. No US State Dept or Lebanese FM statement explicitly declaring the ceasefire void or withdrawn was issued before the horizon. IDF strikes continued in south Lebanon (22 killed in Nabatieh area May 19, six paramedics killed May 22), but the ambiguity rule explicitly excludes IDF strikes outside Beirut governorate and individual violations from resolving YES. The Soufan Center described the ceasefire as existing ‘in name only’ as of May 22, but no formal governmental breakdown declaration was issued. The IDF chief’s statement ‘there is no ceasefire’ is an operational characterization, not a formal government declaration per resolution criteria. Post-horizon escalation (31 killed in 100+ IDF strikes May 27) does not retroactively change the resolution.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if the US State Department or Lebanese Foreign Ministry issues a public statement explicitly declaring the ceasefire void or withdrawn; OR if IDF and Hezbollah resume sustained exchange at pre-April-16 intensity (>50 launches/day from each side) and both US and Lebanon acknowledge breakdown. Individual violations — which are continuous — do NOT resolve YES.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: US State Dept press release or named spokesperson; OR Lebanese government official quoted in Reuters/AP/AFP; OR combined IDF/LBAF situation reports showing pre-truce intensity levels.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: IDF strikes in south Lebanon outside Beirut governorate = NOT collapse (consistent with current porous-truce pattern). Hezbollah verbal threat to resume without acting = NOT collapse. Collapse requires formal withdrawal of US or Lebanese government support.

indicators.name: IDF airstrike on Beirut governorate within 72h of ceasefire extension
indicators.expected_effect: +20pp toward YES; would demonstrate US tolerance for truce violation at capital level.

indicators.name: Hezbollah rocket barrage >50/day from south Litani
indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES; mass rocket fire historically triggers Israeli large-scale response and truce void.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu formally announce an early election date earlier than the mandatory 2026-10-27 date before EOD 2026-06-01?
forecasts.delta_reason: Updated 0.22 → 0.08. The dissolution bill passed a 110-0 preliminary reading on May 20, but the trajectory reversed within days. Haaretz (2026-05-24) reports Degel HaTorah and Shas have aligned with Netanyahu’s preferred October 27 timeline after Netanyahu revived the Haredi draft exemption bill as a side payment. No House Committee discussion has been scheduled for the dissolution legislation. Netanyahu privately told ultra-Orthodox leaders that September elections would ‘endanger’ the right-wing bloc’s prospects; sources describe Haredim as now ‘inclined to accept’ October 27. The formal announcement required — Netanyahu naming a specific date, or a final (third-reading) Knesset dissolution vote — is structurally unlikely within 4 remaining days.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Netanyahu makes a formal Knesset speech or public announcement naming an election date earlier than 2026-10-27; OR if the Knesset passes a formal dissolution motion by majority vote. Leaks and media speculation do NOT resolve.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Times of Israel, Haaretz, or Channel 12/13 news citing direct Netanyahu statement or official Knesset vote record. Reuters/AP confirmation required for international sources.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Coalition partner threatening dissolution without a formal Knesset vote = NOT resolved. Netanyahu ‘considering’ elections per aides = NOT resolved. Only a formal announcement by Netanyahu himself or a passed dissolution vote counts. First or second reading of a Knesset dissolution bill does NOT count as a passed dissolution motion; only final passage (third reading) by majority vote resolves YES.

forecasts.question: Will Iran and the United States sign or jointly confirm a written Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) ending active hostilities before EOD 2026-06-12?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assignment. F3 (June 5 horizon) is too narrow given the May 27 White House ‘complete fabrication’ dispute and Trump ‘won’t be rushed’ statement. This forecast extends the window to June 12. Trump stated May 23 the deal is ‘largely negotiated’; 14-point MOU framework reportedly ~90% agreed; Oman and Pakistan actively mediating. Remaining gaps: Hormuz sovereignty language, nuclear sequencing, sanctions relief (‘no dust, no dollars’). A 15-day window provides time for one additional Oman-channel negotiation round.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if Reuters, AP, or AFP report that both the US government (White House or State Dept spokesperson) AND the Iranian government (IRNA or Foreign Ministry) confirm a joint MOU or framework agreement has been signed or formally acknowledged by both parties before EOD 2026-06-12.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Requires simultaneous independent confirmation by ≥2 of: Reuters, AP, AFP, Bloomberg, or official government statements published on state.gov or mfa.ir.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Unilateral claims by either side alone do not resolve YES. Iranian state TV reporting alone does not resolve YES. A ‘deal in principle’ without written confirmation from both principals does not resolve YES. Trump social media posts without Iranian principal confirmation do not resolve YES. If Iran’s Supreme National Security Council formally blocks or delays implementation within 72h of signing = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.question: Will the 45-day Lebanon ceasefire extension formally collapse — as declared void by the US State Department or Lebanese Foreign Ministry — before EOD 2026-06-10?
forecasts.delta_reason: Initial assignment. This forecast replaces F4 (resolved-NO) and addresses the evident deterioration since May 22. As of May 27: IDF struck 150+ targets in Tyre, Nabatieh, Bekaa Valley (31 killed); Hezbollah launched drones at Rosh Hanikra and Shlomi; IDF chief stated ‘there is no ceasefire’; Netanyahu said Israel is ‘deepening our operation.’ Ben-Gvir called for return to large-scale combat on May 25. However, Trump is actively using the ceasefire framework as diplomatic cover for the concurrent Iran MOU process — a formal US void declaration would undermine his Iran deal diplomacy, creating political incentive to preserve the formal framework despite de facto collapse on the ground. The 45-day extension runs through late June, providing institutional inertia against formal termination.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if US State Dept or Lebanese FM issues an official statement explicitly declaring the ceasefire void or ended; OR if both IDF and Hezbollah officially acknowledge in statements that full combat operations have resumed at pre-April-16 intensity, verified by UN UNIFIL or OCHA reporting >50 launches per side per day sustained over 3+ days.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: US State Dept official statement (state.gov), Lebanese FM official statement, or UN UNIFIL/OCHA situation reports, confirmed by Reuters or AP within 24 hours.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Individual IDF strikes, even mass-casualty, do not resolve YES without a formal US or Lebanese void declaration. IDF chief statements about ‘no ceasefire’ do not resolve YES unless accompanied by a formal government declaration. Hezbollah drone attacks without IDF acknowledgment of ceasefire end do not resolve YES.

indicators.expected_effect: +15pp toward YES; linguistic shift in official briefings would precede a formal void declaration.

indicators.name: Lebanese PM or Foreign Minister issues formal breakdown declaration
indicators.expected_effect: +30pp toward YES; would directly satisfy one branch of the resolution criteria.
